tagline: Every turn you survive, the clock ticks further in your favor.
description: Clock is a patient value deck that wins by outlasting the opponent. Growing units get permanently tougher every turn they live, Countdown creatures like Sparkwright deliver a delayed burst of damage and cards, and Reap punishes trades by drawing you extra resources whenever a unit dies nearby.
gamePlan: Survive the early exchanges with efficient blockers, let your Growing and Countdown effects build up, then close with the value you've stockpiled.
playstyle: Think a turn or two ahead — track your Countdown timers and hold up defensive plays like Temporal Ward rather than racing.
winCondition: Grind through the midgame until Countdown payoffs and oversized Growing threats like Boiler King simply outsize whatever the opponent has left.
strengths: Exceptional at winning long, grindy games
Countdown and Growing generate value with zero further investment
Reap turns even losing a trade into card advantage
weaknesses: Slow starts can lose to dedicated aggro before the plan comes online
Countdown effects can be disrupted by removing the unit first
Needs patience — misplays from racing tend to backfire
pros: Rewards good long-term planning over quick reflexes
Card advantage keeps coming in without extra spells
Strong defensive toolkit including Temporal Ward
cons: Vulnerable in the first few turns against fast aggro decks
Countdown clocks can be played around by an attentive opponent
Less exciting if you prefer proactive, aggressive turns
beginnerExplainer: Countdown cards don't do anything the turn you play them — they trigger automatically a set number of your turns later, so plan around the payoff instead of expecting it immediately.

howToPlay.early: Trade defensively and get a Growing unit down as soon as possible so it starts accumulating stats.
howToPlay.mid: Protect your Countdown units and Growing threats from removal; use Reap-triggering trades to keep your hand full.
howToPlay.late: Let Countdown payoffs like Sparkwright's delayed burn swing the game, then close with an oversized Growing finisher such as Boiler King.
